# Run book: Query a catalog

[Run books](README.md) | [User guide](../user-guide/query-a-catalog.md) | [Spec](../specs/query-a-catalog.md)

- [Purpose](#purpose)

## Purpose

Show that any IQueryable endpoint gets filtering, sorting and paging with cost limits and problem details errors.

## Preconditions

- The signed-in user holds the catalog.read right (the admin role).

## Verify

Automatically: `npx playwright test e2e/journeys.spec.ts -g "Query a catalog"` (add `E2E_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8088` to run against the compose stack).

By hand, in the example web application at `/data/query`:

1. **Run the query.** The filter keeps the instruments under 100, sorted by price, highest first; press Run query. Expect: The table lists the matching rows and the number of matches.

## Troubleshooting

**Table 1 — Known problems**

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bad query | The filter names a property that does not exist or exceeds the cost limits | Use Id, Name, Category, Price or InStock and a shorter filter |
| Forbidden | The user lacks the catalog.read right | Sign in with the admin role |

Related framework features: OoBDev.AspNetCore.OData (`[OoBDevEnableQuery]`, `$filter`, `$orderby`, `$top`, `$count`).
